notes: Planned 2026-11-13, no credits spent. 169s of new Seedance clips needed (about 2704 credits at 1080p, 1183 at 720p) plus ~2 credits per keyframe. Hajar and the angel are never shown: their scenes use point of view, objects, light and the people around them.

shots.description: Days pass over the lone tree: shadows sweep around it in a slow timelapse, the waterskin in its shade slowly sagging empty. No people.
The empty waterskin on cracked earth.
Harsh noon under the tree: the cradle cloth trembles and stirs. Only the cloth moves; no child, no figure visible.
Her point of view walking away from the tree toward the nearest rocky hill, Safa. No figure.
POV climbing the rocky slope of Safa, stones shifting, the summit ahead. No figure, no hands.
From the top of Safa: the empty plain. She saw no one.
Hurried POV running across the valley floor, dust kicking up, the far hill of Marwa ahead. No figure.
Hurried footprints running between the two hills.
POV climbing Marwa and turning to look back across the valley toward Safa: empty. No figure.
High wide view of the valley between Safa and Marwa as the sun arcs across the sky: a worn trail of countless footprints back and forth between the two hills.
The hush on Marwa.
Total stillness on Marwa: dust motes hang in the air, a faint glow, as if listening. No figure.
POV from Marwa turning down toward the valley floor, where a soft light glows at a spot near the lone tree.
A column of soft light over the dry ground near the tree; the earth cracks and clear water bursts up. Light and stillness only: no angel, no wings, no figure.
Water filling the little basin of piled sand and stones.
Close: the open waterskin at the edge of the basin as water flows into it, and the spring keeps welling up. No hands.
The spring overflows its basin and starts to run as a little stream across the sand, then gently settles back into the basin. 'It would have been a flowing spring.'
Peace under the tree: the full waterskin, dates, the cradle cloth still and calm in soft light. No figure.
The angel's words: light on the mound, the site of the House, the spring glittering.
The site of the House raised like a small hill; floods pass to its right and left.
A Jurhum caravan comes down the road of Kada' through a mountain pass and makes camp in the lower part of the valley at dusk. Only men in focus.
Jurhum see the bird circling.
Jurhum men on their camels talk and point up at the bird, puzzled: this valley never had water.
Two Jurhum scouts crest a rise and discover the spring glittering by the lone tree; they turn and wave back to the camp.
Her point of view from beside the spring: Jurhum elders approach respectfully, stop at a distance, hands on their chests, asking leave to settle. She is never shown.
Dusk near the spring: cooking smoke rising from new tents, voices and company; the lone tree is no longer alone.
They settle and send for their families: tents pitched around the spring.
